Prevention: Remove or deep plough to incorporate previous crop residue in the soil to kill thrips.
Practice soil solarisation before planting to kill the pupa.
Plant in well prepared fertile seedbed to promote crop vigour
Mexican marigold followed by sunflower. (Mexican marigold attracts thrips from beans.
Orius spp. which feeds on thrips)
Intercrop with onion, garlic, spider plant or coriander to repel the thrips
Preserve natural enemies such as lady bird beetles, Orius, hover flies and
Keep the fields free of weeds and alternative hosts such as wild mustards
Monitoring: Randomly check for thrip damage at the growing tips of the plants before flowering stage
Look for thrips early in the morning before sunrise (i.e. before 9.00am) since they tend to hide inside the flowers or underneath the leaves in high temperatures
Use blue sticky traps to capture adults
Shake the flowers on a white piece of paper to check for presence of adult thrips
Examine leaves for larvae (silvery appearance of the leaves) to act early
Take action when you notice at least 3 thrips per plant
Direct Control: Place blue sticky traps above the vegetative parts of the plants to kill/ reduce their numbers
Restrictions: Good spray coverage is essential as thrips hide underneath the flowers and leaves;
Use recommended rates of insecticides and rotate between chemicals to prevent resistance build-up;
Apply chemicals early in the mornings or late in the evenings and
NEVER on sunny weather to prevent chemical evaporations and thus losses;
Apply insecticides at 50% flowering on the crop
then follow alternating with botanicals after every 8 days to avoid chemical residues on the harvested beans
Interval (PHI) as indicated on the product label; Wear protective clothing when handling chemicals
